name: hcportal_deleteChatMessage
description: Portal twin of hcapp_deleteChatMessage (E9.F1.S13/S14): soft-deletes one chat message — the caller's own, or anyone's in a thread the caller moderates. The rule lives in HC6.nonApi_deleteChatMessage (moderation via HC6.nonApi_mayModerateChat: moderateChat in the kennel, SuperAdmin for global rooms); this SP only authenticates and shapes the reply. Auth: HC6.ValidatePortalAuth with the token bound to the messageId (callerParamString = CAST(@messageId AS NVARCHAR(40))). Deleting an already-removed message succeeds.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Auth: registered portal device. Validated via HC6.ValidatePortalAuth.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Auth: short-lived portal token; its callerParamString is the messageId.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message to delete; also the token's callerParamString. NULL returns 'messageId is required' (checked after auth).

rowsets.name: SuccessEnvelope
rowsets.description: Returned on every path: auth failure, missing messageId, the outcome of nonApi_deleteChatMessage, or the CATCH block.

columns.name: Success
columns.description: 1 when the message is removed (or already was); 0 otherwise

columns.name: ErrorMessage
columns.description: NULL on success. Outcome 3: 'You can delete your own messages. Only a chat administrator can delete someone else''s.' Outcome 2 (not found): 'That message is no longer in the chat.' Auth error text, or ERROR_MESSAGE() from CATCH.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.nonApi_deleteChatMessage: UPDATE HC.EventMessage SET Removed = 1, updatedAt = SYSDATETIMEOFFSET() WHERE id = @messageId AND Removed = 0 (readers return it in their removedId rowset; trgEventMessageActivityCount updates the run card's chat count)
INSERT LOG.GeneralLog with the removed text when a moderator removes someone else's message
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on not found, not allowed, and unhandled errors

codeSmells.issue: Raw database error returned to the user
codeSmells.detail: Line 59: the CATCH returns ERROR_MESSAGE() as the user-facing ErrorMessage.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
